history.summary: Kapileshwar Temple in Belagavi (formerly Belgaum), Karnataka, is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Kapileshwar and is revered as Dakshina Kashi, the Kashi of the South. Tradition holds that the swayambhu (self-originated) lingam was established by Sage Kapila Muni. Inscriptions in Kamal Basti within Belgaum Fort are cited as dating the temple to about 1000 AD, though another source gives 1204 AD — the founding date is CONFLICT (verify). Devotional tradition says Adi Shankara visited in the 8th century, and Swami Vivekananda, Mahatma Gandhi (1924) and Bal Gangadhar Tilak are said to have had darshan here — treat these visits as traditional claims rather than verified history. The temple stands beside the Shahpur flyover between central Belagavi and Shahapur; a rare cluster of banyan, peepal and ficus trees grows in its compound. name: Kapileshwar Temple
town_description: Belagavi (formerly Belgaum) is a historic city in north-western Karnataka on the foothills of the Western Ghats, near the borders with Maharashtra and Goa. Its fort, dating to the 12th-century Ratta dynasty, and its blend of Kannada, Marathi and Goan cultures make it a major commercial and educational centre. The city is noted for its Shiva temples, including the ancient Kapileshwar Temple and the Army-maintained Military Mahadev Temple.
